title: Nutritional Responses to Acute Exercise Performed on the LipoxMax in Obese Adolescents
official: Nutritional Responses to Acute Exercise Performed on the LipoxMax in Obese Adolescents
summary:
Primarily over the past 20 years, it has been shown that physical activity not only leads to energy expenditure but can also indirectly influence energy intake and feelings of hunger in both lean and obese adults, suggesting that physical activity has a dual effect on energy balance.

Studies in children and adolescents are less common, but it now seems clear that their energy intake is affected by physical exercise ) depending on their weight status.

interventions.name: The participants in this study are adolescents with obesity (with a Body Mass Index above the 95th percentile on international growth charts)

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adolescents aged 12 to 16 (inclusive), at Tanner stage 3-5,
* With obesity defined as a body mass index (BMI) above the 95th percentile according to international growth charts,
* Adolescents enrolled in the social security system or an equivalent program,
* Adolescents who have been informed and have provided written consent to participate in the study

Exclusion Criteria:

* Refusal to participate in the study,
* Refusal of consent by legal guardians,
* Regular use of tobacco or alcohol,
* Special dietary restrictions,
* Participation in regular and intense physical and sports activities,
* Medical or surgical history deemed by the investigator to be incompatible with the study,
* Diabetes, or any other condition that limits the application of either strategy in the trial,
* Adolescents currently following a calorie-restricted diet or a weight-loss program involving physical activity at the time of enrollment or within the past 6 months,
* Taking medications that may interfere with the study results,
* Adolescents with cardiovascular problems; this refers to participants with a history of cardiovascular and/or neurovascular disease, as well as those with cardiovascular and/or neurovascular risk factors (excluding obesity or being overweight),
* Surgery within the previous 3 months,
* Adolescents who are currently excluded from another study,
* Pregnant or breastfeeding adolescents,
* Adolescents under guardianship, conservatorship, or judicial protection,
* Parents under conservatorship, guardianship, or judicial protection
